Thank you. Together, we will keep fighting for a government that truly serves the people.
I’m proud to support Summer’s visionary legislation like the _Abolish Super PACs Act_ , the _OLIGARCH Act_ to tax billionaires, the _Reparations Now Resolution_ to recognize that the U.S. government has a moral and legal obligation to provide reparations for Black Americans, and the _True Justice Act_ to take on our country’s racist and classist cash bail system and ensure everyone’s right to due process.
Summer has also applied my team’s model of constituent service centers throughout her district—helping people access Medicare, Social Security, housing, immigration support, and more.
One of her constituents explained: _“After three tough years of going round in circles with the IRS, I found a real-life superhero team in Summer Lee and her staff... In just one month, Summer’s team did what seemed impossible... It wasn’t just about getting my money and fixing a tax mess at no fault of my own, it was about being heard and helped in a system that felt so defeating.”_
Another constituent wrote: _“After months of battling bureaucratic nightmares with Social Security and feeling helpless, my outreach to Summer’s team became the light at the end of a very dark tunnel... I felt seen, heard, and genuinely cared for.”_
**This is the kind of representation and support that all people deserve.** Summer and I are not only defending vital programs like Medicaid and Social Security, we’re also pushing to expand and improve life-saving services so more people can access them more easily.

clean_body: I’m fighting alongside Summer Lee for our collective liberation. | | | Friend, Israel’s Prime Minister Netanyahu is actively committing war crimes throughout the Middle East, and for years he has been trying to get the U.S. to go to war with Iran—with the help of a foreign lobby organization called AIPAC (the American Israel Public Affairs Committee). AIPAC donates to the vast majority of Congressmembers, and now AIPAC is pressuring these Congressmembers to vote against the wishes of their constituents by supporting yet another endless war. One of the strongest anti-war voices in Congress is Representative Summer Lee , who overcame millions of dollars in attacks from AIPAC and Trump-supporting billionaires to become the first Black woman to serve Pennsylvania in Congress. She recently said: “ It’s disturbing how many warmongers there are in Congress —on both sides of the aisle.” Summer is one of the few members of Congress to keep speaking out for Palestinians’ rights, and now she’s co-leading a historic policy to withhold the transfer of offensive weapons to Israel. Polls show that most Americans want our government to stop arming Israel’s genocidal military. Congresswoman Summer Lee is also a fierce supporter of my anti-war legislation, including a bill to ban members of Congress from investing in weapons corporations—so they actually serve their constituents rather than their stock portfolios. We’re urging our colleagues to join us in supporting the new War Powers Resolution that would stop Trump from going to war with Iran. Instead of sending U.S. troops and taxpayer dollars toward mass death, we’re demanding our government invest in people’s needs at home. | Thank you. Together, we will keep fighting for a government that truly serves the people. I’m proud to support Summer’s visionary legislation like the Abolish Super PACs Act , the OLIGARCH Act to tax billionaires, the Reparations Now Resolution to recognize that the U.S. government has a moral and legal obligation to provide reparations for Black Americans, and the True Justice Act to take on our country’s racist and classist cash bail system and ensure everyone’s right to due process. Summer has also applied my team’s model of constituent service centers throughout her district—helping people access Medicare, Social Security, housing, immigration support, and more. One of her constituents explained: “After three tough years of going round in circles with the IRS, I found a real-life superhero team in Summer Lee and her staff... In just one month, Summer’s team did what seemed impossible... It wasn’t just about getting my money and fixing a tax mess at no fault of my own, it was about being heard and helped in a system that felt so defeating.” Another constituent wrote: “After months of battling bureaucratic nightmares with Social Security and feeling helpless, my outreach to Summer’s team became the light at the end of a very dark tunnel... I felt seen, heard, and genuinely cared for.” This is the kind of representation and support that all people deserve. Summer and I are not only defending vital programs like Medicaid and Social Security, we’re also pushing to expand and improve life-saving services so more people can access them more easily. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime. Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? Every day, I start right here at the kitchen table. It’s where I read through emails, jot down meals for the week, and catch up with my daughter and husband about the day ahead.

It’s a rhythm that’s carried me through every stage of my life. As a little girl, I'd eat my breakfast at the kitchen table in our trailer with my parents before school. In college, I took a moment to myself at my table every morning before running off to class or one of my jobs. **Last week, I sat at this table and launched my campaign for Congress.**

To me, the kitchen table represents more than routine. It’s where families across Iowa talk about the future, figure out how to make ends meet, and remind each other of what really matters. This slab of wood represents staying connected to what matters.

_That’s what Mariannette Miller-Meeks doesn’t seem to understand._

She’s more interested in what Washington insiders and party bosses think than what Iowa families need. While she’s playing political games in D.C., real people are sitting around their kitchen tables wondering if their leaders are paying attention.

I'm here and ready to listen, Peter. My values are rooted in the real lives of working Iowans — families like mine and maybe like yours. I’m ready to bring that experience to Congress and fight for the future we all deserve.

subject: We're crossing the finish line, Peter! 🏁
body:
Hi Peter,
It's the last week of session, so I want to make sure you saw my last email. Things are down to the wire, and we've still have lots to do to get our priorities across the finish line
It's not possible with your support. Make an urgent donation now and help us get our priorities across the finish line! [https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2?am=20&contactdata=h4QRGXtbQqMPGhWhksDObbk0nDTWl+XtNiXgbJ+EdmJNKLzd3qIFYVuSaFTezq4KQTm6gE/NNIgVaq7taJzeNlaw57OUpjZ6eXD2eDzIs32UcW69tIrvAA2UiZCORwXU]

With gratitude,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Sarah%20Signature.png]
Sarah Kline (she/they)
OLCV Communications & Membership Coordinator
P.S.: If you’d no longer like to receive fundraising emails, please use this link here [https://secure.everyaction.com/p/24dczWT--Uqtcu_3MxYYog2] to log-in and update your email preferences.
https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2?am=20&contactdata=h4QRGXtbQqMPGhWhksDObbk0nDTWl+XtNiXgbJ+EdmJNKLzd3qIFYVuSaFTezq4KQTm6gE/NNIgVaq7taJzeNlaw57OUpjZ6eXD2eDzIs32UcW69tIrvAA2UiZCORwXU [https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2?am=20&contactdata=h4QRGXtbQqMPGhWhksDObbk0nDTWl+XtNiXgbJ+EdmJNKLzd3qIFYVuSaFTezq4KQTm6gE/NNIgVaq7taJzeNlaw57OUpjZ6eXD2eDzIs32UcW69tIrvAA2UiZCORwXU]
Dear Peter,
Each day we’re nearing the end of the wire of this year’s session. The Legislature will adjourn by June 29th or possibly sooner. With the climate and environmental attacks we’re seeing at the federal level, this session is critical for our state to deliver on our environmental values. Will you show your support of our priority bills for a healthy Oregon now for these final days of session? [https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2]
Show your support [https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2?am=20&contactdata=h4QRGXtbQqMPGhWhksDObbk0nDTWl+XtNiXgbJ+EdmJNKLzd3qIFYVuSaFTezq4KQTm6gE/NNIgVaq7taJzeNlaw57OUpjZ6eXD2eDzIs32UcW69tIrvAA2UiZCORwXU]
I’m happy to report that the POWER Act ( HB 3546 [https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2025R1/Measures/Overview/HB3546] ), one of our priorities in the Energy Affordability and Utility Accountability package, recently passed and is now headed to the Governor’s desk to be signed into law! We’re still working hard to get One Stop Shop 2.0 ( HB 3081 [https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2025R1/Measures/Overview/HB3081] ) and Get the Junk Out of Rates ( SB 88 [https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2025r1/Measures/Overview/SB88] ) across the finish line before session ends but time is running out.
Safeguarding Streamflows to Protect Oregon’s Water ( SB 427 [https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2025R1/Measures/Overview/SB427] ) was one of our priority bills this session and would have been the most significant progress for Oregon’s streams and rivers in decades. Unfortunately, the bill stalled in the Senate Rules Committee. However, we’ve since pivoted to support SB 1153 [https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2025R1/Measures/Overview/SB1153] , which addresses the same problems and prohibits harm to fish. SB 1153 is an important step forward in modernizing our water laws and we are pleased to see tribal consultation as part of this bill. Nevertheless, it will still take a big effort to get it across the finish line as it is currently stuck in the legislature.
After a long wait, the transportation package ( HB 2025 [https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2025R1/Measures/Overview/HB2025] ) finally dropped a couple weeks ago. While it includes several investments that we advocated for, it does not include everything necessary to meet the needs of our communities and to achieve our climate goals. However, a new amendment has been added to the bill which would provide funds for investments in transportation electrification and community paths and help us meet some of our goals but that amendment is not likely to move forward and the package does not currently move us forward on climate.
Make an urgent donation now and help us get our priorities across the finish line! [https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2] https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2?am=20&contactdata=h4QRGXtbQqMPGhWhksDObbk0nDTWl+XtNiXgbJ+EdmJNKLzd3qIFYVuSaFTezq4KQTm6gE/NNIgVaq7taJzeNlaw57OUpjZ6eXD2eDzIs32UcW69tIrvAA2UiZCORwXU [https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2?am=20&contactdata=h4QRGXtbQqMPGhWhksDObbk0nDTWl+XtNiXgbJ+EdmJNKLzd3qIFYVuSaFTezq4KQTm6gE/NNIgVaq7taJzeNlaw57OUpjZ6eXD2eDzIs32UcW69tIrvAA2UiZCORwXU]
This session has been a whirlwind, but we haven’t let up in the fight for a healthy Oregon. In these final crunch days, we’re going above and beyond to assure that we can get our priorities across the finish line. We can't afford to let up this session and let Oregon backslide.
To get the job done and keep this strong momentum going, we need one more thing: your support. Will you make a contribution of any amount today, so that we can end this session strong? [https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2]
Renew your membership [https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2?am=20&contactdata=h4QRGXtbQqMPGhWhksDObbk0nDTWl+XtNiXgbJ+EdmJNKLzd3qIFYVuSaFTezq4KQTm6gE/NNIgVaq7taJzeNlaw57OUpjZ6eXD2eDzIs32UcW69tIrvAA2UiZCORwXU]
The clock is ticking on this session, but we’re not going anywhere until we get our priorities across the finish line. We can’t do this without you! [https://secure.everyaction.com/TDc4a2r_QEugjeZtF01ipw2]
Thank you for your support,

Will you show your support of our priority bills for a healthy Oregon now for these final days of session? Unfortunately, the bill stalled in the Senate Rules Committee. However, we’ve since pivoted to support SB 1153 [] , which addresses the same problems and prohibits harm to fish. SB 1153 is an important step forward in modernizing our water laws and we are pleased to see tribal consultation as part of this bill. | | Today marks three years since the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_ and ripped reproductive health care and bodily autonomy away from millions of women in America. And these last three years have exposed the true horror of the far-right's crusade against the constitutional right to privacy. Women have been denied the health care they need in emergency rooms, putting their lives in danger. Some have even died. Doctors have had to make impossible choices between doing the jobs they swore an oath to do, or facing criminal prosecution. Families have been forced to flee their home states to get medically-urgent reproductive care. **Now, with a Republican administration in place and the GOP controlling both chambers of Congress, the outlook for reproductive freedom is even more dire than it was in 2022.** Trump recently rescinded guidance that directed emergency rooms to provide emergency abortion care. He pardoned anti-choice protestors who'd been found guilty of harassment and violence outside of health clinics. He revoked Defense Department funding for service members who need to travel to receive abortion care. Meanwhile, Republicans in Congress are taking steps to legislatively chip away at reproductive rights – starting with their budget bill. **One of its many horrible features is a complete defunding of Planned Parenthood.** But there's one fundamental truth that anti-choice Republicans forget: the American people don't sit quietly when their rights are taken away. Time and time again these last three years, we've seen record turnout in down-ballot races against anti-choice extremists. Voters in "red" states such as Montana, Ohio, Kentucky, and Kansas have defeated abortion bans or passed abortion protections. Just two-and-a-half months ago in Wisconsin, with abortion rights potentially on the line, the GOP's effort to retake the State Supreme Court failed spectacularly (with their candidate losing by _ten points_). There is a path to restoring reproductive freedom _everywhere_ in America – and it starts with flipping the House and Senate in 2026. If we do that, we can stop any piece of anti-choice legislation in its tracks and block Trump from appointing more anti-choice extremist judges. **And when a Democratic administration (hopefully) takes office in 2029, our majorities will be ready to immediately restore the rights that**** _Roe_****granted.** Our fight ahead won't be easy, but it can be won. Freedom is a powerful thing – and voters in red, blue, and purple states alike want it. So let's get to work. [**Will you join me? clean_body: Freedom is a powerful thing. | | | | Today marks three years since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade and ripped reproductive health care and bodily autonomy away from millions of women in America. And these last three years have exposed the true horror of the far-right's crusade against the constitutional right to privacy. Women have been denied the health care they need in emergency rooms, putting their lives in danger. Some have even died. Doctors have had to make impossible choices between doing the jobs they swore an oath to do, or facing criminal prosecution. Families have been forced to flee their home states to get medically-urgent reproductive care. Now, with a Republican administration in place and the GOP controlling both chambers of Congress, the outlook for reproductive freedom is even more dire than it was in 2022. Trump recently rescinded guidance that directed emergency rooms to provide emergency abortion care. He pardoned anti-choice protestors who'd been found guilty of harassment and violence outside of health clinics. He revoked Defense Department funding for service members who need to travel to receive abortion care. Meanwhile, Republicans in Congress are taking steps to legislatively chip away at reproductive rights – starting with their budget bill. One of its many horrible features is a complete defunding of Planned Parenthood. But there's one fundamental truth that anti-choice Republicans forget: the American people don't sit quietly when their rights are taken away. Time and time again these last three years, we've seen record turnout in down-ballot races against anti-choice extremists. Voters in "red" states such as Montana, Ohio, Kentucky, and Kansas have defeated abortion bans or passed abortion protections. Just two-and-a-half months ago in Wisconsin, with abortion rights potentially on the line, the GOP's effort to retake the State Supreme Court failed spectacularly (with their candidate losing by ten points). There is a path to restoring reproductive freedom everywhere in America – and it starts with flipping the House and Senate in 2026. If we do that, we can stop any piece of anti-choice legislation in its tracks and block Trump from appointing more anti-choice extremist judges. And when a Democratic administration (hopefully) takes office in 2029, our majorities will be ready to immediately restore the rights that Roegranted. Our fight ahead won't be easy, but it can be won. Freedom is a powerful thing – and voters in red, blue, and purple states alike want it. # [](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/203?t=1&akid=443%2E181023%2E4jjFet)
Team — Today is a tough anniversary for so many women and families in this country.
**Three years ago today, the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_. This decision was a devastating blow to freedom — one not in line with the will of the people, nor achieved through democratic means.**
This decision did not, and still does not, reflect who we are as Americans.
What _is_ a reflection of who we are is how millions of warriors nationwide rose up, spoke out, and fought back. We said, _not on our watch will you take away our rights_. I was proud to be part of the Women from Michigan who helped enshrine reproductive freedom in Michigan’s constitution.
But that’s not the end of our work — it’s only the beginning. And this work is deeply personal to me.
Eight years ago, I had a miscarriage. I struggled with shame and guilt, as so many women who experience the same thing do.
And in this experience, I realized that we need to not just protect reproductive freedom and rights, but **actually make sure they’re real.**
When I needed care, I had doctors and a supportive family that kept me safe, but too many families today, especially in rural areas, don’t.
**Reproductive rights don’t mean anything without access.** As governor, I will make sure every woman, no matter her zip code or income level, can access reproductive health care. Everyone deserves the right to make these personal decisions in private with their healthcare providers — not with the involvement of politicians or judges.
This story is not easy to share. But I want to tell my story to help say that it’s OK to tell yours as well. And because it's time to turn rights on paper into real care for everyone. That is what I will do as governor.
Thank you for reading my story,
Jocelyn

Peter,
When the headlines feel endless and confusing, that's not an accident, it's a tactic. In just the last few weeks, Donald Trump launched unauthorized airstrikes against Iran. ICE raids are intensifying across the country. The military is being deployed to stifle constitutionally protected protest. And Republicans in Congress are pushing a budget that slashes Medicaid and SNAP--taking food and healthcare away from the very people they claim to represent. The foundations of our democracy aren't just cracking. They're being drowned in a flood of chaos, cruelty, and calculated silence. We know it's overwhelming. And we also know that most people don't have time to sort through headlines, statements, and legislative votes every day. **That 's why we send these emails. ** Not just to fundraise, but to bring you clarity. To name what is happening, to offer context, and to speak plainly when others refuse to. **Because you won 't get that honesty from my opponent, Marie Gluesenkamp Perez.** The truth is you can't offer your constituents clarity when you're constantly looking out for political cover. Every vote, every silence, every carefully worded op-ed is filtered through what a consultant thinks will play best in a swing district. And when that becomes the priority, you lose any sense of straightforward, down-to-earth representation. You lose the truth. You end up with a so-called Democrat who won't explain why she refuses to co-sponsor a bill that simply reaffirms Congress's constitutional war powers. Who won't take responsibility for voting with Trump to scapegoat immigrants and fuel a climate of fear. **And who, nearly five days after an unauthorized U.S. bombing campaign, still hasn 't said a single word to the people she claims to represent.** We are not doing that here. This campaign is about bringing you the facts. Not the spin. We are here to help you understand what's happening and what it means. Peter – three years ago today, the Supreme Court stripped women of the constitutional right to end a pregnancy by reversing Roe v. Wade.
**And in these three years since the Dobbs __ decision, the horrors of our new reality have only grown every day.**

Now that 19 states have heavily limited or outright criminalized abortion – for women who seek it in state or out, those who try to help them get it, and medical providers who perform it – **1 in every 3 women of reproductive age in America has no say in the matter.**
🔴 One in three women has to beg judges and politicians for rights that their mother and grandmother once had.

🔴 One in three women must brave life-threatening complications – if they don't succumb to them, like Josseli Barnica, Amber Nicole Thurman, and Candi Miller did last year – since providers can't treat them for fear of prosecution.
All while Donald Trump and the GOP push to gut Medicaid, secretly defund Planned Parenthood, rip away access to safe medication abortion, appoint anti-choice extremists to go after doctors and punish women for seeking essential reproductive care, remove medical privacy protections for pregnant women who cross state lines to get an abortion in states where it is legal, and eventually, end reproductive freedom for women nationwide.
**But we cannot give in. We can – and we _must_ – restore abortion rights for every woman in America.**
Even when state Republicans try to keep referendums off the ballot and rig vote thresholds to protect their unpopular agenda (like in Florida), or use misleading language on the ballot and then outright ignore the outcome to keep voter-rejected abortion bans in place (like in Missouri) the truth that the American people are with us is undeniable: **because almost every time voters get a say, abortion rights win the majority vote.**
I will keep fighting with everything I’ve got to ensure women in every state can make their own health care decisions, free from interference by politicians. Anything else is fundamentally un-American.
So Peter, I urge you to keep using your voice, using your vote, and fighting for everyone's right to receive essential health care, too – because our greatest strength is in numbers. **And together is the only way we win.**

| [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110184241/553544351/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjU3ZDY2NWQ1LTRlNTEtZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=suukjda9oraGAdjIdIuHuYApmVxko_2zI_x3R15SkrE=&emci=0d40f5f9-3a51-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=57d665d5-4e51-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=8431045)

Hey Peter — you hear a lot from us about the dangers of the SAVE Act, which now awaits a vote in the Republican-controlled Senate. We’ve been clear that it’s **one of the biggest threats to voting rights in a generation.** Undermining the power of voters is part of the same far-right playbook that aims to manipulate electoral maps all to stay in power. **But democracy survives only if enough of us believe in it and are willing to fight back against attacks like this.** That starts with each of us doing more to make sure people know what’s at stake in this fight. The NDRC has put together a quick Q&A to help everyone talk to their circles about the SAVE Act. Let’s dive in. **What exactly is the SAVE Act, and why is it so dangerous?**
The SAVE Act, otherwise known as the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, is a bill that would require documentary proof of citizenship in person to register to vote. It could make exercising your right to vote much more difficult if you go through any normal life events. If you got married and changed your last name, or if you don’t have a passport, or maybe lost your original documents in a move or natural disaster, you will have extra hurdles to jump to make your voice heard. **Who would be impacted the most by the SAVE Act?**
The SAVE Act would disenfranchise millions of Americans by throwing up major obstacles to voting that would directly impact working-class Americans, rural voters, victims of natural disasters, naturalized citizens, military members, tribal citizens, married women, LGBTQ+ voters, and people of color. **Are these kinds of voting obstacles being introduced on the state level as well?**
Yes, Republicans in state legislatures are pushing similar bills and have even passed some in recent years. In Kansas, a 2011 proof-of-citizenship law blocked over 31,000 eligible voters, and nearly one in eight new voters. In New Hampshire, married women and countless others were turned away for lacking updated documents when the state legislature removed the opportunity for voters to sign an affidavit at the polling place if they didn’t have sufficient documents. And in Arizona, thousands of voters are effectively shut out of in-state elections due to a strict proof of U.S. citizenship requirement for voter registration. These voters tend to be young, nonwhite, and low-income, meaning that state lawmakers are effectively shutting down the power of certain voters. **Can we still stop the SAVE Act from being passed?**
There are various ways for us to reject the SAVE Act. As a constituent, you can demand your senator vote NO on the SAVE Act — [**take a few minutes to make a call to your senators using our tool.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110184243/553544355/-765811456?contactdata=OdxHnixGByfFq6GdtCzMP8NrOp430jcK/OK9rhsDUkR3Ztd5urDsSVM80SLaWGmxF7S310Z4xeaIGY7/AZX4EqBdO/b6/XGZaxUV0dNoVLEl5gAhJYIbXbZ3zmfCibdE+flW+nCc2PNpIFg2y6TTDA==&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjU3ZDY2NWQ1LTRlNTEtZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=suukjda9oraGAdjIdIuHuYApmVxko_2zI_x3R15SkrE=&emci=0d40f5f9-3a51-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=57d665d5-4e51-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=8431045) But all of us have a role to play in helping shine a spotlight on nefarious legislation like this. By talking about it with your friends, you can help sound the alarm on the dangers of the SAVE Act and build a stronger opposition to legislation like this. In the long run, that’s how we defeat an anti-democracy playbook. clean_body: Sometimes, talking politics can be tough, but this one matters. The NDRC is here to help. | Hey Peter — you hear a lot from us about the dangers of the SAVE Act, which now awaits a vote in the Republican-controlled Senate. We’ve been clear that it’s one of the biggest threats to voting rights in a generation. Undermining the power of voters is part of the same far-right playbook that aims to manipulate electoral maps all to stay in power. But democracy survives only if enough of us believe in it and are willing to fight back against attacks like this. That starts with each of us doing more to make sure people know what’s at stake in this fight. The NDRC has put together a quick Q&A to help everyone talk to their circles about the SAVE Act. Let’s dive in. What exactly is the SAVE Act, and why is it so dangerous? The SAVE Act, otherwise known as the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, is a bill that would require documentary proof of citizenship in person to register to vote. It could make exercising your right to vote much more difficult if you go through any normal life events. If you got married and changed your last name, or if you don’t have a passport, or maybe lost your original documents in a move or natural disaster, you will have extra hurdles to jump to make your voice heard. Who would be impacted the most by the SAVE Act? The SAVE Act would disenfranchise millions of Americans by throwing up major obstacles to voting that would directly impact working-class Americans, rural voters, victims of natural disasters, naturalized citizens, military members, tribal citizens, married women, LGBTQ+ voters, and people of color. Are these kinds of voting obstacles being introduced on the state level as well? Yes, Republicans in state legislatures are pushing similar bills and have even passed some in recent years. In Kansas, a 2011 proof-of-citizenship law blocked over 31,000 eligible voters, and nearly one in eight new voters. In New Hampshire, married women and countless others were turned away for lacking updated documents when the state legislature removed the opportunity for voters to sign an affidavit at the polling place if they didn’t have sufficient documents. And in Arizona, thousands of voters are effectively shut out of in-state elections due to a strict proof of U.S. citizenship requirement for voter registration. These voters tend to be young, nonwhite, and low-income, meaning that state lawmakers are effectively shutting down the power of certain voters. Can we still stop the SAVE Act from being passed? There are various ways for us to reject the SAVE Act. As a constituent, you can demand your senator vote NO on the SAVE Act — But all of us have a role to play in helping shine a spotlight on nefarious legislation like this. By talking about it with your friends, you can help sound the alarm on the dangers of the SAVE Act and build a stronger opposition to legislation like this. name: Lizzie Fletcher
subject: Three years without Roe.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS
body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
It’s been three years since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade —and changed life for millions of women across America, undermining their health, dignity, and freedom.
Since the Dobbs decision issued three years ago today, nearly one-third of all women of reproductive age now live in states that have banned abortion. In Texas, we’ve seen some of the most extreme restrictions enacted—restrictions that put women’s lives, health, and futures at risk.
We’ve heard heartbreaking stories of women facing life-threatening pregnancies, only to be denied care or turned away entirely. We’ve heard stories of women who cannot get care when having miscarriages, which are all too common. We’ve heard stories of women sent to wait at home or in the parking lot until they are closer to dying so that they can get care. These are not isolated incidents—they are the direct and devastating consequences of cruel abortion bans.
Doctors and healthcare providers in Texas and 18 other states that have banned abortion are working in stressful environments where state laws create fear and uncertainty and threats of losing their medical licenses or going to jail for providing health care are all too real. Hospitals are delaying emergency care while legal teams review the cases.
We know that in states like Texas, fewer doctors are being trained. And pregnant women are facing greater risks than they have in decades.
Instead of working to fix this crisis, the Trump administration is making it worse. The agenda we’re seeing play out—in state legislatures, in courts, and in Congress—is exactly what extremists, politicians, and special interest groups set out to achieve: to take away reproductive freedom, to undermine women’s autonomy, and to insert politics into the most personal, private decisions a person can make.
But I believe—as the vast majority of Texans and Americans do—that these decisions belong to patients and their doctors, not politicians.
This work is so important—and it’s why I’m asking for your support today. We can elect pro-choice leaders in Texas and across the country. But we can’t do it without resources. It will take all of us, working together, to deliver the message to voters and show them what we are fighting for: freedom.
If you’re in a position to give, please consider making a contribution to our effort today. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe250624dobbs?refcode=lpfe250624dobbs]
In 2026, we have a chance to take back the House majority. And retaking the House is essential to protecting our rights, safeguarding our democracy, and ensuring that future generations of Americans have more freedom, not less.
These last three years have brought so many challenges, in Texas and beyond. But I continue to be inspired every day by the courage, passion, and determination of so many people in our community and across our country who refuse to give up. I’ve seen what we can do when we work together.
Together, we can do anything,

Peter,

Three years ago today, a Trump-packed Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade:_ The right to abortion care.

This historic, devastating decision marked the beginning of a plethora of anti-abortion legislation from extreme lawmakers all across the nation.

From Florida's six-week ban to Texas' cruel and unusual bounty hunter law–which allows private citizens to sue doctors or anyone involved in helping a woman access abortion care–**American women have lost their autonomy, safety, privacy, and even their lives because they are now unable to access basic, fundamental healthcare.**

Peter, I want to be crystal clear about something: Abortion IS healthcare. It's a procedure that not only saves lives, but also allows women to have control over their own bodies. No judge and no legislator should ever have the right to tell you—or anyone else seeking medical care—what to do with your body. **This is especially important when a pregnancy is no longer viable or could cost a woman her life.**

This issue is not going away. As drafted now, Trump's "One Big, Beautiful Bill” defunds Planned Parenthood and prevents Affordable Care Act insurance policies from paying for abortion care. Meanwhile, states across the country are enacting even more serious bans with no exceptions for rape, incest, or the life of the mother.

As a doctor, I took an oath to protect your health, and as your Congresswoman, I took an oath to protect your rights. No matter what kind of agenda Trump and his extremist allies try to push, I will always fight for your right to make your own healthcare choices. Healthcare decisions should be made by patients and their doctors. Not Trump, not a conservative Supreme Court, and not politicians.

Even though three years have passed, we cannot forget about the women who have already suffered. clean_body: Peter, Three years ago today, a Trump-packed Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade: The right to abortion care. This historic, devastating decision marked the beginning of a plethora of anti-abortion legislation from extreme lawmakers all across the nation. From Florida's six-week ban to Texas' cruel and unusual bounty hunter law–which allows private citizens to sue doctors or anyone involved in helping a woman access abortion care–American women have lost their autonomy, safety, privacy, and even their lives because they are now unable to access basic, fundamental healthcare. Peter, I want to be crystal clear about something: Abortion IS healthcare. It's a procedure that not only saves lives, but also allows women to have control over their own bodies. No judge and no legislator should ever have the right to tell you—or anyone else seeking medical care—what to do with your body. This is especially important when a pregnancy is no longer viable or could cost a woman her life. This issue is not going away. As drafted now, Trump's "One Big, Beautiful Bill” defunds Planned Parenthood and prevents Affordable Care Act insurance policies from paying for abortion care. Meanwhile, states across the country are enacting even more serious bans with no exceptions for rape, incest, or the life of the mother. As a doctor, I took an oath to protect your health, and as your Congresswoman, I took an oath to protect your rights. No matter what kind of agenda Trump and his extremist allies try to push, I will always fight for your right to make your own healthcare choices. Healthcare decisions should be made by patients and their doctors. Not Trump, not a conservative Supreme Court, and not politicians. Hi Team, it's Jane.

Republican Senator Mike Lee has spent years attacking the values we hold dear, and now, he’s back with another dangerous proposal.

He recently attempted to include a provision in the latest Senate draft of Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill” that would require the federal government to sell off up to 3.3 million acres of public land to state and local governments across 11 Western states.

Fortunately, massive public outcry and a ruling from the Senate Parliamentarian has forced him to abandon his original proposal, but he is committed to including a public land-sale provision in this bill. We can’t let that happen.

While he’s working on the exact language of his newest proposal, **[we need you to keep up the pressure and reach out to your senators today and demand they reject any new sales of public lands in this legislation.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110185287/553547671/1866710405?refcode=ea.a7edfa29-5351-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ms=ea.a7edfa29-5351-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImE3ZWRmYTI5LTUzNTEtZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=tTLz3aGLAIlB_es_EybjS1kXsPR5m1K5fiAFe65eP24=&emci=39b596c5-4d51-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=a7edfa29-5351-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=4823105)**

Public lands aren’t just landscapes. They’re places where families hike, fish, and hunt. They’re some of the few remaining places people can find connection with the natural world. Not to mention, they serve as some of the last remaining habitat for wildlife already impacted by over-development and the changing climate.

This land belongs to the people. It shouldn’t be sold off to pay for tax cuts for billionaires and corporations.

clean_body: | Hi Team, it's Jane. Republican Senator Mike Lee has spent years attacking the values we hold dear, and now, he’s back with another dangerous proposal. He recently attempted to include a provision in the latest Senate draft of Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill” that would require the federal government to sell off up to 3.3 million acres of public land to state and local governments across 11 Western states. Fortunately, massive public outcry and a ruling from the Senate Parliamentarian has forced him to abandon his original proposal, but he is committed to including a public land-sale provision in this bill. We can’t let that happen. While he’s working on the exact language of his newest proposal, Public lands aren’t just landscapes. They’re places where families hike, fish, and hunt. They’re some of the few remaining places people can find connection with the natural world. Not to mention, they serve as some of the last remaining habitat for wildlife already impacted by over-development and the changing climate. This land belongs to the people. It shouldn’t be sold off to pay for tax cuts for billionaires and corporations. | Public lands belong to all of us. body:
The fight for abortion rights is far from over |
#
---
Folks — Three years ago, the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_ and ripped away a fundamental right from hundreds of millions of Americans. It was a dark day — and since then, the consequences have been heartbreaking. Doctors have been forced to delay life-saving care because of vague or cruel abortion bans. Women have been turned away from hospitals while experiencing dangerous complications. Some have died. Others have had to flee their home states just to get the basic care they need. **Let me be clear: This is the reality that extreme right-wing politicians chose. And they won’t stop here.** That’s why, in Michigan, we took action. Grassroots organizers, advocates, and Michiganders from all walks of life came together to protect reproductive freedom — **and we won.** We passed a ballot initiative to enshrine abortion rights in our state constitution, and we made sure our laws match our values. We’re not the only ones. In states like Kansas, Ohio, and Kentucky, places where you might not expect it, voters have mobilized to protect reproductive freedom and reject extremism. This is a powerful movement. And it’s only growing stronger. But here’s the truth: Those victories, inspiring as they are, still aren’t enough. **Access to abortion shouldn’t depend on your zip code or the whims of extremist lawmakers.** We need to restore the federal protections that _Roe_ once guaranteed — and that means fighting for national legislation to safeguard reproductive freedom in every state. **[Will you add your name today to demand federal protections for abortion care?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110185300/553547713/-114579147?refcode=AU_FLHP_EG_GEN_PET_AC90_20250624_PM2_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY0NjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTI0ZGY1NzUtNTM1MS1mMDExLThmN2MtNjA0NWJkZmU4ZTljIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=XMo0EzGrziZbwPtonk08F4YQf3CesTgWNc1ZZ_DQ9dM=&emci=b6509e90-5051-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=124df575-5351-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=1028753)** | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110185301/553547714/-114579147?refcode=AU_FLHP_EG_GEN_PET_AC90_20250624_PM2_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY0NjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTI0ZGY1NzUtNTM1MS1mMDExLThmN2MtNjA0NWJkZmU4ZTljIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=XMo0EzGrziZbwPtonk08F4YQf3CesTgWNc1ZZ_DQ9dM=&emci=b6509e90-5051-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=124df575-5351-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=1028753)

body:
|
#
---
Peter, the conservative movement spent decades chipping away at _Roe v. Wade._ They lobbied ferociously. They allied with dark-money donors. Anti-abortion Republican presidents packed the Supreme Court with right-wing judges with ideological axes to grind. On June 24th, 2022, the right-wing majority on the Supreme Court finally handed Republicans what they had spent decades working for by overturning _Roe v. Wade_. The _Dobbs_ decision instantly stripped millions of Americans of their right to make their own reproductive health care choices. And it has emboldened GOP-led states across the country to go even further by passing laws that criminalize doctors for providing essential, life-saving care — without exceptions for cases of rape or incest. **This was the first time in American history that the Court had _taken_ _away_ a constitutional right from the people, Peter.** Now, Republicans are working to enact an abortion ban nationwide and control every aspect of women’s reproductive care. It doesn’t matter that Trump waffled on the issue of a nationwide abortion ban during his campaign — when Republicans hand him this bill, he will sign it and every woman in America will face a new world with less rights. My Democratic colleagues and I are still fighting every day for reproductive justice — and we will not stop. But we need to elect even more Democrats to the Senate who will restore and protect reproductive freedom. **[Donald Trump and his Republican allies aren’t showing any signs of slowing down in their efforts to ban abortion nationwide, which is why it’s on us to stop them. name: Deb Haaland
subject: Most people running for office wouldn’t choose to speak candidly about alcohol addiction.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO
body:
I want to tell you about a milestone I’m proud of
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=2804%2E400544%2EqKLw_b)
I want to tell you about a milestone I’m proud of: **I have reached 35 years of sobriety.**
Most people running for office wouldn’t choose to speak candidly about alcohol addiction. But I’m not like most people running for office. My story is different.
I was about 23 years old when I made the brave decision to get sober. It was a struggle at first, but I persevered because I was committed to doing all I could. I went to AA meetings and probably read 20 books on addiction.
My struggles made me fierce, which is why I chose to speak openly about my sobriety in my very first campaign ad when I ran for Congress, which aired 7 years ago. And I’m so glad I did. I'll never forget the day we went to the Marigold Parade in the South Valley, and people came up to me right and left and thanked me for saying that in my ad. They shared stories about themselves, their parents, and their loved ones struggling with addiction, and it brought tears to my eyes that people felt represented by someone like me.
**My journey to sobriety taught me that you must face hard truths if you want to make change, which is why I’ll never shy away from the tough fights that lie ahead for New Mexico.**
Crime, poverty, homelessness, and addiction are weighing heavy on our state, and I intend to tackle those challenges head-on as governor. I promise to be honest about topics other politicians might try to sweep under the rug, because I believe if we’re brave, we can heal.
Thank you for hearing my story. That’s how we’ll win this race — by sharing our stories, lifting each other up, and being fierce enough to fight for the bright future New Mexicans deserve. Thank you for everything.
Deb

subject: NEWS: Pushing hospitals to comply with emergency abortion care obligations
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ROB BONTA FOR CALIFORNIA ATTORNEY GENERAL 2026 FPPC ID #145642]
body:
[ https://act.robbonta.com/go/4?refcode=em250624&t=1001&akid=1844%2E1088799%2EF4_wPW ]Rob Bonta

Three years ago today, the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade.

Every day since, far-right politicians have done everything they can to
strip away fundamental rights — including trying to deny pregnant patients
lifesaving emergency care.

That’s against the law.

We aren’t letting them get away with this. Today I co-led a coalition of
22 attorneys general who sent a letter to the American Hospital
Association urging hospitals across the country to comply with EMTALA —
the federal law that guarantees access to emergency medical care,
including abortion care.

Refusing that care endangers the lives of pregnant people everywhere,
leading to unnecessary suffering and death.

As Attorney General, I will continue using every legal tool available to
hold hospitals accountable and defend access to emergency abortion care —
because these decisions belong to patients and their healthcare providers,
not politicians or administrators.

We can’t let up — but our end-of-quarter fundraising deadline is coming up
fast, and my re-election campaign relies on grassroots donations to keep
us in the fight.
